observations.title: Helm, GitOps, And Infrastructure Configuration · KubeClaw Documentation
observations.accessibilityTreeExcerpt:
- main:
  - article:
    - heading "Helm, GitOps, And Infrastructure Configuration" [level=1]
    - group: Page scope and sources
    - heading "Summary" [level=2]
    - paragraph: This page presents an inventory snapshot of scalars, lists, and maps in chart defaults, checked-in overlays, GitOps values and manifests, release values, and infrastructure manifests. Open a file section to inspect its nested fields. The inventory redacts credentials, identities, and access lists. A redacted value remains configurable, but this page never publishes its content.
    - heading "Select And Verify A Change" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Find the owning file below. Chart values are defaults; a checked-in overlay is not automatically selected by every command.
      - listitem: Read the receiving source and precedence column. Direct deploy uses generated release values and its optional selected overlay. Production GitOps selects immutable bundle resources through its Application source.
      - listitem: Change the owning input, not a generated release copy alone. Render the selected chart or regenerate the bundle through the linked producer. Inspect the affected workload, Secret reference and policy before applying it.
      - listitem: After the normal deployment, verify the effective resource and process health. Source discovery and rendering do not prove a rollout, API admission, image behavior or cluster policy enforcement.
    - paragraph: "Scope: all YAML inputs currently discovered under charts, examples, gitops, my-values and releases/values. The file index records the actual selected membership, not a fixed count. Nested API contracts explain the selected manifest fields; this bounded values reference does not renew unrelated global program-output, environment o

observations.title: Worker Core: From Claim To Durable Result · KubeClaw Documentation
observations.accessibilityTreeExcerpt:
- main:
  - article:
    - 'heading "Worker Core: From Claim To Durable Result" [level=1]'
    - group: Page scope and sources
    - heading "Purpose" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Worker Core runs one bounded attempt. It gives Buster, Prism, and a future specialist engine the same rules for identity, limits, cancellation, logs, evidence, cleanup, and terminal results.
    - paragraph: Worker Core does not decide which pipeline node runs next. Nova owns that decision. Worker Core also does not understand test policy or design policy. The specialist engine owns that meaning.
    - paragraph: This separation is deliberate. A memory limit must have the same meaning for a test process and a design process. A test result and a design result must not have the same domain meaning.
    - blockquote:
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Core boundary
      - paragraph:
        - link "The public package exports attempt mechanics, native process controls, ownership, trust helpers, and contract digests":
          - /url: https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ce7740252864a9b547bee8a35260d6ab10c9f05e/skills/worker/core/src/index.ts#L1-L52
        - text: .
      - paragraph:
        - link "The operation interface keeps specialist execution behind prepare, execute, terminate, measure, cleanup, evidence, and finalization hooks":
          - /url: https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ce7740252864a9b547bee8a35260d6ab10c9f05e/skills/worker/core/worker/attempt-executor.ts#L30-L93
        - text: .
    - heading "The Two Execution Layers" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Worker Core has two related execution layers.
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Layer Responsibility Does not provide":
          - columnheader "Layer"
          - columnheader "Responsibility"
          - colum

    - paragraph: This separation is deliberate. A memory limit must have the same meaning for a test process and a design process. A test result and a design result must not have the same domain meaning.
